description: Channel version bindings (SPEC §8.3.1 and §8.6, from 0.3.0). Every descriptor version carries, in a `binding` tag, the kind-30078 device record that binds its event pubkey: an OC Lock v3 record for a Bitcoin address, a §8.6 session record with its vouch for a did:oc. A version with a later version after it on the chain is authorized by that binding alone; the last version of a chain also needs its binding to be live (no revocation seen on any relay, the device's own or, for a did:oc, the auth host's). At a fork, and among the geneses of one channel_id, a version the founder signed with a live binding ranks first, one with a binding since revoked second, any other third; a live device's copy of a version counts as that version signed with a live binding. A founder can re-sign a channel with a new genesis for the same channel_id when no version verifies or the inbox-key device is revoked. A retired host key verifies only a vouch issued before its retired_at.

lookup: relay_records is every kind-30078 record the reader sees on any relay. A version event carries its own binding in its `binding` tag; relay_records decide whether the last version's binding is live, and bind a version that has no binding tag (published before 0.3.0). For a did:oc, verify vouches and host revocations against the case's jwks (default jwks_rotated); a retired key verifies only what it signed before its retired_at.

cases.name: an admin revoking its own key does not undo its edit or what follows
a revoked key's own last version falls back to the version before it
before the revocation, a version signed with the stolen key counts
after the revocation it does not; the version re-signed from the live device stands, and the genesis signed with the revoked key stays in the chain
the thief's admin T signs a successor; while the stolen key is live it stands
revoking the stolen key alone does not undo a version a live key has built on
after the revocation, the founder's fork from the live device outranks the stolen key's branch
before the revocation both branches are the live founder's, and the longer wins
the thief forks from the genesis with a stolen non-inbox key and grows a longer branch; without copies it wins
with the live device's copies of the versions the stolen key signed, the founder's branch outranks it
the thief's own genesis, signed with the stolen inbox key, wins on length while that key is live
once the inbox key is revoked, the founder's new genesis from a live device outranks every genesis that key signed
a genesis whose key no record binds does not verify
the founder re-signs it with a new genesis for the same channel_id
a did:oc version vouched under a retired host key still verifies, and its own revocation does not undo it
a version from a stolen session device counts until the auth host revokes the device
after the host revokes it, the channel ends at the version before
a vouch the host issued after revoking the device binds it again; the earlier one stays revoked
a vouch under a retired host key, issued after it was retired, binds nothing
if the host dropped the retired key, that version and every later one fail

notes: admins in expected name the inputs.addresses keys. epochs counts versions from the genesis to the tip. Reproduce with the reader clock at reader_now.
